title: Say "I Love You".
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Mei Tachibana has avoided friendship since she was betrayed and blamed by classmates in elementary school. After she kicks popular Yamato Kurosawa by mistake, he pursues her, and their relationship slowly opens her to friends such as Asami, Aiko and Kai. The story follows their high school years into early adulthood, when Mei works with young children and Yamato becomes a photographer.
life_message: A good life comes from risking trust, letting others in and being loved for who you are.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts over reputation and rumors are resolved through talk and forgiveness, not retaliation.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Teens choose relationships and careers with little adult control.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Chosen friends matter more than family; Yamato's siblings appear but are secondary.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: School popularity hierarchy is questioned; friends treat each other as equals.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern, secular school and fashion world; no religious frame.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Self-acceptance, body image and personal feelings drive the story.

folkways.japan: Group exclusion in class (ijime) and attention to reputation within a school year reflect Japanese school social norms.

delivery.evidence: No source addresses delivery; trust theme carried by Mei's friendships and romance (to verify).
delivery.note: Trust and vulnerability are carried by Mei's growing friendships, with cruelty and rumor as the contrast.

winners_losers: Mei gains friends and love; isolation, cruelty and rumor-mongering lose. Sympathy goes to vulnerability and loyal friendship.
